I have resolved the issue where deferred fields were incorrect when following prefetches back to the "parent" object.

### Cause
When prefetching across a one-to-one or reverse many-to-one relationship (`ForwardManyToOneDescriptor`, `ReverseOneToOneDescriptor`, and `ReverseManyToOneDescriptor`'s `RelatedManager`), `get_prefetch_queryset()` iterates over `queryset` (evaluating any nested `prefetch_related()` / `select_related()` lookups on the related objects) and then unconditionally sets the reverse relation cache on each related instance (`rel_obj`) to the parent `instance` from the outer queryset. When a nested prefetch (or `select_related`) had already populated that relation on `rel_obj` with a custom queryset (e.g. with different `.only()` / `.defer()` fields), the outer `instance` overwrote the cached object.

### Solution
Updated [`ForwardManyToOneDescriptor.get_prefetch_queryset`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-swqauzwy/django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py#L120-L150), [`ReverseOneToOneDescriptor.get_prefetch_queryset`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-swqauzwy/django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py#L365-L383), and [`RelatedManager.get_prefetch_queryset`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-swqauzwy/django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py#L635-L655) in [django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-swqauzwy/django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py) to only populate the reverse relation cache on `rel_obj` if it is not already cached (`not ...is_cached(rel_obj)`).
